newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco stadium to cost $4.6 mln a yr - report.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco stadium to cost $4.6 mln a yr - report.

text.p: A proposed football stadium and retail complex could increase San Francisco's general fund expenditures by $4.6 million annually, according to a report by the city's budget analyst.

The entire project is expected to cost about $537 million, including $250 million for a proposed 75,000 seat stadium for the National Football League 49ers, and $200 million for the proposed entertainment and shopping complex.
The existing 70,000 seat 3Com Park at Candlestick Point would be demolished once the new stadium is completed.
To help finance the project, city officials have proposed a $100 million lease revenue bond issue that would be placed on the June 3 ballot, city officials said.

San Francisco's budget analyst said city expenditures would increase by about $8.1 million annually for debt service and $4 million for the city's share of operations and maintenance at the proposed new football stadium.
These costs would be offset in part with savings from the closure of 3Com Park, and from new sales and gross receipts tax revenues generated at the new project.
The budget analyst said the net effect would be an increase in the city's general fund expenditures by $4.6 million annually.

"This estimate assumes that the estimated $5,000,000 in incremental sales tax revenue that would be producted by the new retail and entertainment mall will be fully realized and not supplant sales tax revenue that the city would receive from other shopping centers," the budget analyst said.
